subject.title: [Feature]: openclaw models status --probe --all — per-model health check across all configured models

question: Should OpenClaw add `models status --probe --all` now as the canonical configured-model health probe, fold it into broader fallback/migration model-safety UX, or defer it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the command makes real provider requests and overlaps related fallback-chain and staged model-migration product surfaces, so automation should not choose the permanent CLI contract alone.

options.title: Approve Bounded Status Probe
options.body: Add `--probe --all` to `models status` as an opt-in all-configured-model health check with explicit cost/rate-limit wording, JSON schema, tests, docs, and real CLI proof.

options.title: Unify With Model-Safety UX
options.body: Keep this issue open while maintainers design one workflow covering all-model health, fallback-chain testing, staged promotion, and rollback.

options.title: Defer Core CLI Surface
options.body: Leave the current auth probe and external dashboard/workaround paths in place until provider diagnostics become a higher priority.

recommendation.title: Approve Bounded Status Probe
recommendation.body: Add `--probe --all` to `models status` as an opt-in all-configured-model health check with explicit cost/rate-limit wording, JSON schema, tests, docs, and real CLI proof.

likelyOwner.reason: He introduced the current auth-probe surface and has the strongest history on the model status/probe code path.
